chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"You supplicate in the Witr prayer against the enemies, and if you wish, you name them, and you seek forgiveness, and you raise your hands in the Witr prayer facing your face, and if you wish, [raise them] beneath your garment."
ai.seo_question: How should one raise their hands and whom should they supplicate against during the Witr prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic flexibility (rukhsah) in the Witr prayer’s Qunut, allowing the supplicant to choose between specific or general invocation against enemies. It further clarifies the physical etiquette of raising hands, offering the option to keep them visible or concealed beneath the garment, reflecting the practical adaptability of Shia ritual practice.
